name: Anchorframe
tagline: One folder per film. Cast as ids, shots as prompts, takes as a board.
promise: Nothing goes to video until it already exists as stills that are right. Every face is attached by id, never re-described. Every take is on a ledger. The cut is chosen from evidence.
derived_from: MATTER OF LIGHT — 5:43, 21:9, 27 shots, made entirely in Higgsfield for the Higgsfield Global Film Festival, Aug 8 – Sep 14 2026. Every number below is that production's, not an estimate.

loop._: The inner loop that runs inside stages 4–6 until the picks are the film.

steps.do: Admit this project's takes — by cast id, by ledger, by hand map. Drop and count the rest.
Run every take ≤16s through the Virality Predictor, two at a time. Free.
Lay the board. Pick by your call, else by score, else newest.
Look, then write pick + alternates into the shot, with why.
Make only what is missing or broken. Ledger on acceptance.
Pull the picks in cut order. Native size ×2 at most. Titles in the NLE.

stages.name: Story
stages.question: What is the film about, and who changes?
stages.goal: A logline, a screenplay, a shot list whose durations sum to the target, and a dialogue cut small enough to be spoken by a machine and believed.
inputs: the rules of the venue (minimum length, format, what must be made inside the platform)
outputs: shot list with durations and acts
dialogue cut (lines per shot, words per second budget)
the turn — which character changes and in which shot
surfaces: writing, not generation — optional Claude for drafting and the seat briefs
steps: Write the logline first; if it needs a second sentence the film has two subjects.
Cut the screenplay to shots at cinema length (mean 13s), not sizzle length (4s). Motivate every cut by point of view, time or revelation.
Cut dialogue to what a synthetic voice can carry: 556 → 89 words here. Mark the shots that are silent on purpose.
Name the turn. The last held close-up belongs to whoever changes.

iterate.name: the ending
iterate.trigger: The turn lands on the wrong character, or lands too late.
iterate.do: Rewrite the last two shots only. Everything upstream survives.
iterate.exit: The logline still describes the film.
iterate.mol: The ending was reversed on Sep 14 — Alder, not Wren, learns the right lesson: “There's something more.” S22 rewritten in all three lanes; nothing else moved.

mol.numbers: 23 shots at 13.0s mean; 3 movements 80/118/102s; 12 lines, 89 words, 6 speaking shots; 3 silent by design incl. the climax

reminders: Logline in one sentence. Two sentences means two films.
Mark the shots that are silent on purpose — now, in the shot list.
Name who changes, and in which shot. The last held close-up is theirs.

stages.name: Cast
stages.question: Does every face, place and thing exist once, by id?
stages.goal: Every character, lighting plate, location, prop, creature and effect generated on a plain background inside the project, each an element with a uuid, each Soul trained once. Nothing downstream describes a face; it attaches one.
inputs: the world's rules written as sheets (here: the aura hierarchy — bright rim/black centre for adepts, bright centre/no edge for bearers)
outputs: cast: characters / environments / props / fx as name → uuid
retired: old name → old uuid, so old renders still attribute
one Canvas board per lighting plate
surfaces: Image (nano_banana_2 / nano_banana_pro) for sheets
Soul Cast (soul_2, budget 10–500) for identities
Elements panel — every handle dragged, never typed
Canvas — one board per plate, shelf row first
Cinema Studio project folder — generate inside it
steps: Rule sheets before any character (the aura rule; the attunement ladder).
Leads: train a Soul, then generate state sheets from it (damaged, ascended, mortal) — never re-describe the face.
Plates: one per act plus one for any lighting exception (the bombardment). Every frame inherits its board's key.
Locations, props, creatures, effects: plain background, three views on one sheet where it helps.
Record every id. Reference as @[name](uuid) in every prompt from here on.

iterate.name: identity
iterate.trigger: A face moved between sheets · a shot used a superseded sheet · an element was replaced in the web app and the repo didn't know.
iterate.do: Retire the old id (record old → new), regenerate the sheet from the Soul, sweep every prompt for the old reference, rebuild.
iterate.exit: Gate A — everything from this stage on one screen; no face moved.
iterate.cost: Images are cheap; a Soul retrain is the expensive one. A missed swap costs a shot later.
iterate.mol: Two swaps happened by hand and went unrecorded (prop_enemy_ships → twelve-ships, courtyard). S5's four takes all carried the mortal Caedom sheet. Seven Souls existed; four match the cast in use; three marked superseded. 32 element ids in the project at lock.

gate.name: Identity lock
gate.test: All sheets on one screen, in the canvas. Look for a face that moved. A gate is a person looking at a screen; record the answer.

mol.numbers: 42 reference sheets · 37 handles · 5 Souls trained (4 active) · 4 plates · 3 boards
mol.dates: Sep 5 done; Gate A held Sep 8

reminders: Every prompt attaches @[name](uuid). Never a described face.
Record old → new the moment you replace an element; sweep every prompt.
One Soul per generation. Two-person shots run on elements.
Generate inside the project folder — the API cannot file it for you.

stages.name: Anchors
stages.question: Does the film exist as stills, in order, that are already right?
stages.goal: Two frames per shot — first and last — generated in film order on the right board, chained from the previous frame. Shared frames end one shot and start the next; bridge frames are near-black hidden cuts; match pairs are two images designed together.
outputs: anchor plan: F01…Fnn with role (single / shared / bridge / match), handles, dependency, job id, url
surfaces: Image, on the board, from the shelf
Canvas — anchors left to right in shot order, spans drawn under them
steps: Generate F01 first: the film's first frame should be almost nothing.
Chain: each frame references the previous frame's job id, not its prompt.
One image doing two jobs (shared) is generated once. A bridge must go genuinely near-black. A match pair is made as a pair.
No text, no watermark, no logo in any frame — say it three ways in the prompt.

iterate.name: the frame
iterate.trigger: A composition will not survive being held for its duration · a shared frame reads as two rooms · a bridge is only 70% black.
iterate.do: Two passes on the prompt, then rewrite it. Promote any draft that beats its anchor.
iterate.exit: Gate B — every frame on one contact sheet, read left to right twice, no drift.
iterate.cost: One image per pass. Drift here costs an image; drift later costs a video.
iterate.mol: 39 frames for 23 shots; skeleton pass one generation each on Sep 6; the selection pass was where time went.

gate.name: String lock
gate.test: The contact sheet. Read it twice. Anything that drifts is regenerated before a single video.

mol.dates: Sep 6 skeleton; selection open through Sep 12

reminders: First and last frame of every shot, in film order, on the plate's board.
Chain from the previous frame's job id, not its prompt.
Say 'no text, no letters, no watermark' three ways.
A bridge frame goes truly black, or it is an honest cut.

stages.name: Stills reel & timing
stages.question: Does it play, at length, before anything moves?
stages.goal: Assemble the anchors at their shot durations and watch the whole runtime as stills. Then freeze runtime, order and count — after this a structural change costs video, not images.
surfaces: any NLE, or the board itself
steps: Cut the stills at duration. Sit through it. Where attention drops is where a shot is too long or a cut is unmotivated.
Decide the structure now: linear, prologue splice, fold, interlace. Price each in new anchors.
Freeze: runtime, shot order, shot count.

iterate.name: structure
iterate.trigger: The lead dies before the audience has met whoever carries the ending · the peak lands too early.
iterate.do: Move an establishing beat, not a scene. One new anchor at most.
iterate.cost: Cheap here (one anchor), expensive after (re-rendered video).
iterate.mol: Option B — the first five seconds of the brothers' beach placed before the vortex — was priced at one anchor on Sep 8 and finally applied on Sep 14 as an edit-only split of an existing take. Zero generations.

gate.name: Timing lock
gate.test: Runtime, order and count frozen. Any change after this is a re-render.

mol.numbers: 300s target; landed 5:43 with the new shots
mol.dates: planned Sep 9; the split applied Sep 14

reminders: Sit through the stills at duration before anything moves.
Decide the structure now — after Gate C a change is video, not images.
Freeze runtime, order and count. Write the date down.

stages.name: Motion
stages.question: Is every shot a move between two frames that are already right?
stages.goal: Video for every shot, generated inside the project, two takes each, on the model whose ceiling, reference support and audio behaviour fit the shot. Chain start and end frames on anything over 12 seconds.
inputs: the model matrix (duration ceiling · two-frame · audio refs · aspect · folder)
outputs: takes, admitted to the project by cast
surfaces: Cinema Studio — cinematic_studio_video_4_0 (web app; 8–16s; 720p→1080p; 21:9) inside the project
minimax_h3 — the one API model with two frames + audio references + 21:9 + folder_id
Virality Predictor — every take ≤16s, 2 concurrent on the plan, free
MCP connector for batch and history; Cloud API for scripted submission
list_projects / list_folders / list_project_assets (MCP) — project membership, item by item, with folder: what ingest.py admits by first
steps: Read what you are actually using before you spec a run — pull the project's placements and its history. (The notes said v2 · 12s · 720p. The account said v4.0 · 16s.)
Cheap pass on every shot first; finals per act after.
Two takes per prompt. A third take on the same prompt is a different prompt.
Audio off on the shots the shot list marks silent. Audio references, not model audio, wherever there is dialogue.
Every take through the Predictor. Read the curve, not the number.

iterate.name: the take
iterate.trigger: An identity break the model can't see (wrong sheet) · a shot that exists only as a chroma lane · a beat with no take at all · a score that is a clear outlier against its pair.
iterate.do: Regenerate only that: the corrected prompt, the same references, the right sheet. Ledger on acceptance. Re-ingest, re-score, rebuild.
iterate.exit: Gate D — motion lock: every shot has a pick you would ship.
iterate.cost: ~5 min and one video credit per 16s take at 1080p. Scoring is free.
iterate.mol: 59 takes admitted of 130 in the account; 18 scored; 17 of 18 peaked on their last second; S5 flagged (mortal Caedom), S14 single take, S10 dragon-dead pair excluded, four new shots written and unshot at deadline.

gate.name: Motion lock
gate.test: A pick per shot, chained where it must be, no identity break in any pick.

mol.numbers: 51 v4.0 renders Sep 10–14 · durations 8/12/14/16 · 1344×576 at 720p · 2 of 16 chained · 540 credits left
mol.dates: Sep 8 cheap pass (seam shots); Sep 13 the big run (43 renders); Sep 14 the last pair

reminders: Pull the history before you spec a run. Read what you are actually using.
Two takes, then rewrite the prompt.
Chain start/end frames on anything over 12 seconds.
Audio off wherever the shot list says silent.
Score every take ≤16s. Read the curve, not the number.

stages.name: Voice & sound
stages.question: Is every sound in the project, and is every silence a decision?
stages.goal: Dialogue generated per line, several takes each, chosen for the scene's mood and routed into the shots as audio references. Score and sound design made wherever is honest, then every file uploaded into the project.
outputs: every audio file in the submission project
surfaces: seed_audio (0.1 credit/line; speech_rate −50..100, pitch −12..12; no seed)
text2speech_v2 / ElevenLabs-via-Higgsfield (3 fields)
qwen_audio_tts (the one with a real seed + instruction)
Suno for score (no API — app, then upload)
steps: Cast two candidates per character on the same line; pick; write it down.
Four takes per line with mood settings from the scene. Keep the spec take as take 1.
Route: generate the voice first, attach it as an audio reference on a model that accepts one, turn the model's own audio off on that shot.
Credit music honestly on the end card. Keep the rights receipt.

iterate.name: the read
iterate.trigger: A line reads flat against its picture · a take is the wrong tempo for the shot's duration.
iterate.do: One more take at ±12 speech rate. Never more than four per line; choose.
iterate.exit: Every speaking shot has one selected take and it is in the project.
iterate.cost: 0.1 credit a take. The cheapest thing in the production.
iterate.mol: 12 lines · 40 takes · Kiki and Alistair · 2 speaking scenes silent by design incl. the climax; the S1 narration existed but was not under the black at submission.

mol.numbers: 40 voice takes · 4 per line · 0.1 credit each

reminders: Generate the voice first; attach it as an audio reference; model audio off on that shot.
Never more than four takes per line — choose, and write it down.
Every audio file uploaded into the project before you submit.
Credit the music honestly on the end card. Keep the rights receipt.

stages.name: The cut
stages.question: Which take, in what order, and why?
stages.goal: The board: one pick per shot, alternates beside it, the continuance from first shot to last. Cut on the tail, never the head. Selection is the grade. Fix structure with edits before generations. End-card plate generated; end-card type in the NLE.
outputs: pull-picks.sh — the picks in cut order + a rough assembly
surfaces: the board
DaVinci Resolve (assembly, titles, sound — permitted outside the platform)
Cinema Studio for anything that is picture
steps: Pick by look, tie-break by score; write why under each pick.
Trim from the head. 17 of 18 takes paid on their last second.
Where a chroma take and a flat take exist, the chroma take is the grade. No colour pass across two lighting worlds in an hour.
Timeline resolution = the film's aspect before export, or the bars bake in. 2560×1098 · 24 · H.264 CRF 17 · AAC 320.
End card: generate the plate with no text (say it three ways); lay the credits in the NLE at 12s+.

iterate.name: the cut
iterate.trigger: A read of the scores against the judges: an arc problem (who changes and when), a light problem (drift, a flat take), a hook problem (a silent first three seconds).
iterate.do: Three changes, one per judge, priced in generations — prefer the zero-generation edit (a split, a voice under black, a take swap).
iterate.exit: Gate E — picture lock. Nothing is generated after it.
iterate.cost: Minutes. The whole point is to spend edits, not credits, this late.
iterate.mol: Change 1: the brothers' first 5s before the vortex (edit only). Change 2: cut on the tail; S22 on the chroma take (59 vs 49). Change 3: the S1 narration under the black; NEW-2 the one generation worth starting.

gate.name: Picture lock
gate.test: No further generation. The export exists and plays end to end.

reminders: Trim from the head, never the tail.
Chroma take over flat take. No colour pass across two lighting worlds in an hour.
Timeline aspect = film aspect before export, or the bars bake in.
End-card plate generated with no text; end-card type in the NLE.

stages.name: Deliver
stages.question: Does it count?
stages.goal: Rights pass, watermark and packshot from inside the platform, a public post on a public account, every file verified inside the project, submitted before the deadline in the deadline's own timezone.
outputs: the public post (and its logged-out check)
posts and descriptions for X / Instagram / YouTube
a support email on file if anything errored
the published project page — film, prompts and history, public
surfaces: Cinema Studio submit flow (watermark + packshot)
the contest page
YouTube / X / Instagram / Reddit
support@ / contact@ / Discord
steps: Rights: end card credits the source and the AI audio honestly; no real face or voice anywhere in the inputs.
MVS 1 — watermark + packshot applied by the platform's own flow, never recreated.
MVS 2 — public post, public account, checked in a private window.
Verify every generation is inside the project. Submit. Then stop.
Deadline in its own timezone. Two files in this repo disagreed (UTC vs PT). Work to the earlier one.

iterate.name: none
iterate.do: This stage is a checklist, not a loop.
iterate.cost: Zero if the rules were read on day one.
iterate.mol: Watermark question answered at 21:17 UTC on deadline day; final MOV at ~23:30; the recorded deadline had passed by the next check. Posts, loglines and support contacts were prepared the day after.

mol.numbers: MVS = 2 components · 3 support addresses verified · 3 loglines ≤140 · published at https://higgsfield.ai/@drawingsquid1334/projects/matter-of-light

reminders: Watermark and packshot from the platform's own flow — never recreated.
Public post AND public account. Check both in a private window.
The deadline in its own timezone; two records disagreed here — work to the earlier one.
Verify every generation is inside the project. Submit. Stop.

expand._: The same primitives, three products. What changes is scale and the shape of a 'shot'.

feature.name: Anchorframe Feature
feature.scale: 1 project per act or per sequence sharing one cast file · 20+ boards · a continuity audit that runs across projects · a stills reel per act
feature.status: roadmap — needs: multi-project cast sharing, cross-project ingest, an act-level board, per-scene ledgers

series.name: Anchorframe Series
series.scale: 1 project per episode · one cast file with per-episode overrides
series.status: roadmap — same as feature plus a season board

play.name: Anchorframe Play
play.scale: cast → character sheets, turnarounds, expression sheets · plates → level key art and lighting · shots → cutscenes · takes → animation and sprite variants · the board → asset review · the ledger → provenance for every shipped asset
play.status: roadmap — needs: a sheet type per asset class, an export to engine folder structure, and a review board keyed by asset rather than by shot

unique.d: Faces, places and things are attached, never described. A rename cannot break a reference; a retired element is recorded, not forgotten.

unique.k: Provenance you can hand to a jury
unique.d: Every take the desk makes is on a ledger before anyone waits for it. Admission to a project is by cast, not by folder — which is the only thing the API can actually enforce.
Every take scored; the curves read against what a jury sits there to see. The cut is chosen with numbers on the table and a person making the call.
Five gates, each a person looking at a screen, each recorded. Nothing downstream begins until the gate above holds.

course._: The living course: each stage shows examples from a finished project with what to look for, and a reminders checklist that remembers your ticks in this browser. Any project can add examples.json beside its project.json and they appear here, labelled.
